clue.text: 14's actor Bob, after taking part of Theseus, was the conductor

indicators.note: the actor's name comes after the piece taken from Theseus
only a portion of the word Theseus is wanted, its opening letters

parts.note: Bob Peck was an English stage and screen actor
a conductor led the band, read here as two words

explanation.surface: A tale of an actor called Bob who played a bit of Theseus and then took up the baton.
explanation.walkthrough: 14 is CONAN DOYLE, so '14's' means one of his Sherlock Holmes stories.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a Sherlock Holmes short story written by Arthur Conan Doyle, the writer at 14.

clue.text: 14's first gripper, negative element with mini-trauma?

parts.note: A is the first letter and grade, the top
a stud on a boot sole gives grip
yin is the passive, negative principle in Chinese philosophy
a small scar would be a scarlet, as a droplet is a small drop

explanation.surface: A description of some odd items: a grip, a negative ingredient and a minor injury.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the invented word: the diminutive ending -let attached to scar.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the first Sherlock Holmes novel, written by Arthur Conan Doyle, the writer at 14.

clue.text: Campaigning for a straight delivery?

definitions.meaning: a politician out canvassing support is said to be giving stump speeches
in cricket a straight ball aimed at the wickets is bowled at the stumps

explanation.surface: A politician canvassing for votes is likened to a bowler aiming straight.
explanation.walkthrough: The stumps are the three upright sticks of a cricket wicket; a bowler's delivery heading at them is straight.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes a politician touring to make speeches during an election campaign.

clue.text: In love with glue?

definitions.meaning: glue is what something attached by adhesive has been fixed with

explanation.surface: A whimsical question whether being in love is like being glued.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means infatuated with someone, and literally describes something fixed by adhesive.

clue.text: Despicable people on top

definitions.meaning: froth or impurities that float on the surface of a liquid

explanation.surface: Unpleasant people who have risen to the top.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is slang for worthless people and also names the film of impurities floating on liquid.

clue.text: 14's left man, possibly dead, for three miles at sea

parts.note: red is a label for the political left
he is the male pronoun

indicators.note: possibly means the letters could take another form, so they are rearranged

parts.note: a league is an old measure of about three nautical miles

explanation.surface: A leftist man, maybe dead, lost three miles out at sea.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a Sherlock Holmes short story by Arthur Conan Doyle, the writer at 14.

clue.text: 14's clue for thin leaf — but more followed after resurrection

parts.note: these two words are the rearranged letters of the title's first two words, and the title's last word works as the signal to rearrange them, so the title is a clue for them

explanation.surface: A remark about a story that was meant to end things but was followed by more after a revival.
explanation.walkthrough: THE FINAL rearranged gives THIN LEAF, with PROBLEM as the anagram signal. The tail recalls that Holmes died in this story but Conan Doyle resurrected him for more adventures.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the Sherlock Holmes story in which Holmes apparently dies at the Reichenbach Falls.

clue.text: Body parts — the old story

parts.note: the chest is part of the body
nut is slang for the head

explanation.surface: Some anatomy alongside a tale from long ago.
explanation.definitionFit: A chestnut is a stale joke or anecdote told too many times.

clue.text: Loveless heart, then no start to suffering nursery

indicators.note: love is O in tennis scoring, so the O comes out

parts.note: core means heart, the centre

indicators.note: the first letter of the synonym is dropped

parts.note: ache means pain or suffering

explanation.surface: A heartless loveless figure causes misery at a nursery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Loveless' takes O from CORE to leave CRE; 'no start to' takes A from ACHE to leave CHE.
explanation.definitionFit: A creche is a day nursery where young children are looked after.

clue.text: Fool to turn to church qua church

parts.note: an ass is a foolish person
a U-turn, so U stands for turn

explanation.surface: A fool converts to the church, considered purely as a church.
explanation.walkthrough: The closing 'church' only completes the phrase 'church qua church', showing how qua is used.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin qua means in the capacity of, considered in itself, matching this phrase.

clue.text: Return of Scot (don't tell anyone) behind in engine

indicators.note: return means the word is turned back to front

parts.note: Mac is a familiar name for a Scotsman
sh is a call for quiet and secrecy
aft means at the back, behind

explanation.surface: A secretive Scotsman lurking behind an engine.
explanation.definitionFit: A camshaft is a rotating shaft with cams found inside an internal combustion engine.

clue.text: Drink, say, for a lot of 19s, say

definitions.meaning: a variant spelling of bevvy, slang for an alcoholic drink
19 is a songbird; a collective term for a group of such birds

explanation.surface: Having a drink while watching a flock of birds.
explanation.walkthrough: BEVVY is British slang for a drink, sometimes spelt with one V.
explanation.definitionFit: A bevy is a group of birds such as quails or skylarks, and also slang for a drink.

clue.text: Vices (including, today, tea) which have a grip

indicators.note: the vices word contains the other pieces

parts.note: vices are sins
now means at present, today
cha is slang for tea

explanation.surface: A list of vices that today happens to include tea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'including' puts NOWCHA inside SINS. 'Vices' suggests clamping tools, which fits the grip, but here they are sins.
explanation.definitionFit: Snow chains fit round tyres to give vehicles traction on icy roads.

clue.text: Writer opposed, with love, to see rising

parts.note: con means against, as in pros and cons
and means together with
love is zero, O

indicators.note: in a down entry rising means read upwards, back to front

parts.note: Ely is a cathedral city and bishop's see in England

explanation.surface: An author who is against seeing things rise, but with affection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' turns ELY into YLE. A see is the seat of a bishop.
explanation.definitionFit: Arthur Conan Doyle was the writer who created Sherlock Holmes.

clue.text: A lot of booze going below interrupts the brain endlessly

indicators.note: breaking into a word means being put inside it
the final letter of the synonym is dropped

parts.note: the skull is the brainpan, standing for the brain
inf is short for infra, Latin for below

explanation.surface: Drinking too much gets into your head and dulls the brain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' leaves SKUL; 'interrupts' places INF inside it. 'going' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A skinful is as much alcohol as a person can hold, enough to get drunk.

clue.text: German student in any case has a bad-tempered old style

indicators.note: the pieces are put inside the word that acts as the case

parts.note: the word any forms the case, the outer shell
L is the learner plate, a student driver

explanation.surface: A German student who is bad-tempered in any case.
explanation.definitionFit: Angerly is an archaic adverb meaning in an angry way, so bad-tempered in an old style.

clue.text: Step outside hotel into boat

indicators.note: the step word goes round the other piece

parts.note: a pace is a step
an inn is a hotel

explanation.surface: Stepping out of a hotel into a boat.
explanation.definitionFit: A pinnace is a small boat carried by a larger ship.

clue.text: Preparatory notice affected how things were seen

indicators.note: affected means altered, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: prep is short for preparatory, as in prep school

explanation.surface: An advance notice that changed how events were viewed.
explanation.walkthrough: PREP plus NOTICE gives the letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Perception is the way something is regarded or understood.

clue.text: Early rising sport

definitions.meaning: the skylark sings at dawn and soars upward
fun or a prank, a bit of a game

explanation.surface: Getting up early for a game.
explanation.definitionFit: The lark is a dawn singer, and a lark is also a bit of fun or mischief.

clue.text: A flower in a Swiss city, a granite one

indicators.note: the river goes inside the city name

parts.note: Bern is the Swiss capital
something that flows, a river; the Dee is a river

explanation.surface: A flower blooming in a Swiss city made of granite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flower' is the crossword river, one that flows. Aberdeen is known as the Granite City.
explanation.definitionFit: Aberdeen in Scotland is nicknamed the Granite City for its grey stone buildings.

clue.text: Circulator to bear losing head

indicators.note: the first letter of the synonym is dropped

parts.note: a teddy is a toy bear

explanation.surface: A bear losing its head in a circulating current.
explanation.definitionFit: An eddy is a swirl of water or air that circles round.

clue.text: Eggs mob's thrown at Namibian

parts.note: ova are eggs

indicators.note: thrown means the letters are tossed into a new order

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written

explanation.surface: A mob hurling eggs at someone from Namibia.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ovambo are a people of northern Namibia, so the word names a Namibian.

clue.text: Mean to do home nursing?

parts.note: in means at home
to tend is to nurse

explanation.surface: A plan to provide home nursing care.
explanation.definitionFit: To intend something is to have it as a purpose, to plan to do it.

clue.text: No philistines can be like pearls

definitions.meaning: people refined in taste, not boorish
pearls grown by farming are of this kind

explanation.surface: Refined people compared to farmed pearls.
explanation.definitionFit: Cultivated people are refined, and farmed pearls are grown with human help.
